title: Activation Brief — Velocity Thermostat
content:
Purpose:
This brief synthesizes the launch readiness posture for the upcoming feature activation (customer-facing API routing changes + new quantized model bundle). It introduces the 'Velocity Thermostat' — an operational control set that ties real-time KPI thresholds to automated traffic shaping and escalation steps. Use this doc as the single source for go/no-go signals during the 14-day ramp and initial 72-hour surge window.

Scope and Assumptions:
- Applies to Hosted API and Dedicated pools only (Private deployments excluded).
- Canary window will target 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% traffic phases.
- Capacity numbers assume average payload length 60 tokens and peak concurrent requests distribution per region (US/EU).
- Rollout target start: 2025-03-10 (T-28). Dates here are placeholders for scheduling.

Quick Status Heatmap (green / yellow / red):
- Model bundle verification: green (matrix tests pass, conversion logs clean).
- Load test baseline (simulated 100k qps-equivalent): yellow (CPU tail spikiness observed at sequence >512).
- Observability retention for token-level breakdown: green.
- On-call staffing coverage for 72-hour surge: yellow (need one more SRE night shift).
- Legal/compliance signoff for telemetry: green.

KPI Suite (owner / current / target / action-if-breached):
- P99 latency (generation end-to-end) / Owner: Evan Park / Current: 210ms / Target: <=180ms / If >220ms for 15m -> throttle canary + route to fallback quantized variant.
- Error rate (5xx) / Owner: Marisol Ortega / Current: 0.6% / Target: <=0.3% / If >1% for 5m -> pause rollout and initiate rollback playbook.
- Token cost per 1k tokens (USD) / Owner: Product Finance / Current: $0.043 / Target: <=$0.035 / If >$0.05 for 1h -> enable batching suggestions and reduce batch timeouts.
- Throughput (tokens/sec per GPU) / Owner: Serving Runtime / Current: 9k / Target: >=10k / If <8k persistently -> shift traffic to Dedicated pool reserved nodes.
- Adoption conversion (trial->paid within 14d) / Owner: Growth / Baseline: 12% / Target: 18% / Monitor but not gate for launch.

Velocity Thermostat: Control knobs and thresholds
- Thermostat inputs (real-time): P95 latency, P99 latency, 5xx rate, queue length, GPU utilization, cost burn rate.
- Control outputs: canary traffic pct, batch-window ms, KV-cache TTL extension, model-variant fallback, region failover flag.
- Example rule: If P99 > 220ms AND GPU util > 85% -> reduce new canary traffic by 50% and increase batch-window by 25ms.
- Escalation tiers: advisory (ops slack alert), protective (auto-adjust thermostat), critical (auto-pause rollout + on-call page).

Launch Readiness Checklist (must be completed before T-3 to proceed):
- [ ] End-to-end smoke tests (happy path + long prefix): owner: QA (Automations).
- [ ] Canary pipeline runbook checked into Console (routes set, policy IDs): owner: Product.
- [ ] Observability dashboards built (token breakdown, gen-time waterfall, model delta view): owner: Observability.
- [ ] On-call rotation confirmed for surge window with named backup: owner: SRE.
- [ ] Capacity reservation for first 30 days (Dedicated buffer 20%): owner: Capacity Planning.
- [ ] Billing alerts configured for unexpected cost spikes: owner: Finance/Growth.
- [ ] Customer comms draft ready for org (support + CSM templates): owner: Customer Success.
- [ ] Compliance checklist signed (PII telemetry filters validated): owner: Security & Compliance.

Capacity & Deployment Notes:
- Initial reserved pool: 40 GPUs in us-west-2, 20 GPUs eu-west-1 for first 72h.
- Burst policy: auto-burst to offsite Dedicated nodes up to +30% for 2 hours, requires ops approval at +50% sustained.
- Estimated token burn at 100%: 23M tokens/day (peak day) -> budgeted unit cost estimate included in linked artifacts.
- Warmup plan: run synthetic prefix caching for 6h before canary open to reduce cold-KV effects.

Canary Procedure (detailed steps):
1) T0: Deploy model bundle to canary hosts (test-only flag). Run 1k synthetic requests, confirm KV cache warming and no deserialization errors.
2) T+30m: Open 0.1% traffic; monitor KPI suite for 30m.
3) If stable -> 1% for 60m. If stable and thermostat readings good -> 5% for 2h.
4) Between 5% -> 25% ramp: run incremental A/B quality checks (top-line hallucination rate, rerank regressions).
5) At each step any critical breach -> execute rollback playbook and route traffic to previous stable variant.

Rollback Playbook (top-level):
- Immediate: flip routing policy to stable model variant (hot path cached), notify on-call and product ops.
- 5m: Run fail-forward diagnostics (compare request samples, check kernel selection logs).
- 15m: If unresolved, scale Dedicated capacity and open incident channel.
- 60m: Postmortem ownership assigned by product ops lead.

Communications and Stakeholder Matrix:
- Incident comms owner: Marisol Ortega (ops lead) -> use incident template in Slack #prodops-incidents.
- Customer-facing comms: Customer Success owner: Priya Shah (drafted templates in linked artifacts).
- Exec updates cadence: 2x daily during first 72h surge (09:00 PT, 21:00 PT).

Signoff Matrix (must be signed before T-1):
- Product Manager: Asha Menon (yes/no)
- Serving Runtime Lead: Evan Park (yes/no)
- Observability Owner: Jinsoo Park (yes/no)
- SRE Lead: Tara Nguyen (yes/no)
- Security & Compliance: Liza Moreno (yes/no)

Open Questions / Risks:
- Long-tail sequences (>1024) show latency variance in staging. Action: schedule kernel selection review with runtime team (ticket PLAT-2314).
- One-night SRE gap during T+48–T+60 hours. Action: rotate backup and confirm pager duty override.
- Billing threshold sensitivity for partner customers not fully scoped. Action: Growth + Finance to run a partner blast simulation.

Immediate Action Items (next 72 hours):
- Marisol: confirm SRE night coverage and post rota by EOD (+1).
- Evan: re-run load test focusing on sequences 512–2048 and attach tail logs (+2).
- Product Ops: finalize stakeholder comms and signoff spreadsheet (+3).
- Observability: add an alert that ties P99 delta to model-variant rollout id (+2).

Appendix: quick references
- Canary checklist (detailed stepper): confluence:PRODOPS-velocity-thermostat
- Rollback runbook: JIRA:PLAT-2314#/rollback-playbook
- Cost model spreadsheet: github:infra/serving/cost-models#tokens-estimate

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive: the Velocity Thermostat is designed to reduce decision latency during surges and create measurable automated protective actions. Please comment on thresholds and whether any KPI should be escalated to a hard gate.

Last updated by: Asha Menon on 2025-03-02
